name: Bengali
doc: Everything the stroke generators need to know about one script. Stroke vocabulary (roles body/second/struct/accent; junctions red/touch/cross) is shared by all scripts and lives in code.

rule_notes.BAR_Y: Bengali frame: headline y (measured; headroom above it for tall stems and flags)
rule_notes.DESC_Y: short descender height in the Bengali frame (placeholder: not yet measured)
rule_notes.START_AXIS_TOL: measured: only half of Bengali strokes start within 22 degrees of an axis (p90 41), so no axis rule
rule_notes.CUP_OPEN_TOL: Bengali curves open at any angle
rule_notes.LINE_AXIS_TOL: only 5 of 107 Bengali strokes are straight; those are vertical within 2 degrees
rule_notes.VERT_FULL_BOTTOM: vertical stems reach the baseline (85) less 4, as in Devanagari
rule_notes.RELAXED_TOL: a stroke attached at both ends may sit near 45 degrees
rule_notes.MAX_TURN: measured: Bengali strokes turn up to 631 degrees (p90 492) against 560 (p90 358) in Devanagari: curls and loops are normal
rule_notes.MAX_SPAN: loops and long sweeps are normal in Bengali (placeholder)
rule_notes.RING_FRAC: Bengali has closed loops (ha, ī and others): the closed-ring rule is off
rule_notes.JOIN_AT_END_P: chance a second stroke meets the first at its end
rule_notes.SHORT_FIRST_LEN: always at the end if the first stroke is shorter than this
rule_notes.BAR_OVERHANG: bar extends this far past the last contact
rule_notes.INK_MIN_DIST: chamfer distance below which two letters are the same shape
rule_notes.WHITE_MAX: share of frame farther than WHITE_R from ink (review 1)
rule_notes.PRIMARY_MIN: biggest stroke at least this fraction of bar width or height
rule_notes.HALF_INK_MIN_DIST: half-bar letters compared on left form + connector
rule_notes.ATTACH_SLIDE_TOL: sliding an attachment point this fraction along a stroke is not a new letter (review 1)
rule_notes.STROKE_STEM_CLEAR: strokes keep this far from the stem / descender except at junctions
rule_notes.REPAIR_BASE_EXTRA: repair may grow ink this far below the baseline
rule_notes._status: Bengali: frame, drawings and the rules listed here come from measurement (script_config/measure.py). Everything else (clearance and size thresholds, recipes, skeleton, half-bar) is still copied from Devanagari and needs review rounds.
rule_notes.BAR_MIN_WIDTH: measured: Bengali bars are 45-88 wide, median 77 (p10 68); Devanagari 64-73

traits.headline: most letters; not universal (e, ai, o, au, ṅa, ña and others are bar-less)
traits.blue_green: segments of one body sequence, not distinct forms
traits.acute_tips: an orange ring on a 3-branch skeleton fork marks two strokes meeting at an acute tip
